text: dsh-agentic-pet 是 DSH 桌面宠物插件，提供桌宠界面、互动工具和侧边栏设置页。它将宠物页面接入 DSH Web 组合，由本机 Electron 载体展示，并通过驱动跟随会话状态；在宠物预设中，模型可让宠物显示短气泡或执行动作。设置页还能配置宠物选项和可选的 BreezeBlue 语音朗读。适合想在桌面查看并互动的 DSH 用户；语音功能需要 BreezeBlue API Key。

dsh-agentic-pet adds a desktop companion, interaction tools, and a sidebar settings page to DSH. It serves the pet in a local Electron carrier and follows session state. With the pet preset, the model can show a speech bubble or request an action. Optional BreezeBlue voice playback needs an API key.
想让 DSH 在桌面上显示一个会跟随会话状态变化的宠物。
希望能从 DSH 侧边栏调整桌宠行为和语音设置。
Can my DSH desktop companion show a short bubble or perform an action?
dsh-agentic-pet 的功能「桌面宠物互动」：为模型注册宠物表达工具，向桌宠发送简短气泡或动作请求。工具仅在挂载宠物预设且 DSH tools 服务可用时注册。
dsh-agentic-pet 的功能「语音朗读设置」：在桌宠设置页填写 BreezeBlue API Key、选择声音并启用语音；宠物说话气泡可以由外部 TTS 服务合成语音。
dsh-agentic-pet 使用 BreezeBlue TTS 时会把气泡文本发送至 api.breeze.blue 合成语音；需在设置页提供 API Key，代码说明密钥保存在本机设置文件。

description: "The dsh desktop pet: an agentic pet plugin that serves the pet renderer over the web composition, drives it from in-process dsh events, and answers approvals and questions from the desktop."
kind: "package-bundle"

dsh-agentic-pet README · dsh-agentic-pet：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

dsh-agentic-pet README · Summary：`dsh-agentic-pet` is a desktop-pet plugin for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) ecosystem: the pet lives on your desktop as a transparent always-on-top window, follows your agent sessions (idle / thinking / working / error), races the web GUI to answer approvals and user questions (first answer wins), collects a per-pet touch-affection ledger, and exposes expressive tools (`pet_say`, `pet_do`, `pet_digest`, `pet_interactions`, `pet_state`) so the model can speak and act through the pet. Spoken lines can be read aloud through [BreezeBlue](https://breezeblue.ai) TTS — the carrier synthesizes each `/say` text and delivers bubble and voice as one event; synthesis failure or timeout degrades to visual-only (configure it in the desktop settings page). Multiple pet implementations can run side by side — a directory registry (`~/.dsh/pet-http.d/`) discovers every live pet and routes state, interactions, and ledgers per pet.

dsh-agentic-pet README · Summary：The pet itself is a dumb display with zero dsh knowledge. Everything that understands the runtime — event convergence, interaction waterfalls, multi-pet routing, the model tools — lives in the plugin's driver, and the pet only implements a small local HTTP control interface. Any pet implementation that speaks the same HTTP contract can be adopted without changing this plugin.

dsh-agentic-pet README · What's in this repo：| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/` | The plugin (Cordis bundle): `/pet` route, event driver, registry, `PetService` seam, model tools, settings-page routes |
| `client/` | The desktop sidebar settings page (client half) |
| `carrier/` | The Electron carrier **build artifacts** shipped with the package (`lib/`, `dist-renderer/`) |
| `carrier-src/` | The carrier **sources** (mirrored from the dev upstream; media assets live in [dsh-pet-assets](https://github.com/beyondgjc/dsh-pet-assets)) |
| `vendor/typert-plugin/` | Vendored typert decorator plugin used by the packaging config |
| `tests/` | Vitest specs (pure-function coverage of the registry routing and the `/status` field-matrix normalization) |

dsh-agentic-pet README · Install：From the DeepSeek Harness desktop app's plugin page, or:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-agentic-pet
```

The animation media ship as a separate package, `dsh-agentic-pet-assets`, and are pulled in automatically as a dependency.
dsh-agentic-pet README · Development：The TypeScript build still runs inside the dsh monorepo workspace (the bundled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` deps are not published to npm). The flow:

dsh-agentic-pet README · Development：1. In the monorepo: `pnpm run build` (plugin `lib/`) and `pnpm --filter @deepseek-ai/dsh-pet run build` (carrier `lib/` + `dist-renderer/`).
2. Here: `scripts\sync-from-monorepo.cmd` — mirrors sources and build outputs into this repo.
3. Commit here, then publish from here (see [Releasing](#releasing); the assets package goes first, manual in [dsh-pet-assets/PUBLISH.md](../dsh-pet-assets/PUBLISH.md)).

dsh-agentic-pet README · Development：Tests: `npx vitest run tests/registry-service.spec.ts` runs self-contained (needs only `cordis` and `vitest`); the full suite including `tests/pet-app.spec.ts` runs in the monorepo workspace.

dsh-agentic-pet README · Releasing：`package.json`'s `version` is owned by this repo: `scripts\sync-from-monorepo.cmd` mirrors every other manifest field and keeps it. The monorepo copy carries the workspace version (`0.2.1-rc.3`), so a plain mirror copy used to rewrite the published number — which is why npm `0.4.0` had no commit and no tag carrying it.

dsh-agentic-pet README · Releasing：```bash
node scripts\release.mjs 0.4.1 --dry-run   # preflight and pack listing, nothing published
node scripts\release.mjs 0.4.1             # publish, commit "chore(release): 0.4.1", tag v0.4.1
git push --follow-tags
```

dsh-agentic-pet README · Releasing：The script refuses to publish unless the working tree is clean, the version exceeds the current one, tag `v<version>` is absent, the build artifacts are present, and `lib/` carries exactly one bundle chunk (`tsdown` runs with `clean:false`, so a stale `service-*.js` would ship). A failed publish restores `package.json`, so the tree never claims a version that did not ship. A prerelease version (`x.y.z-rc.N`) publishes under `--tag rc`.

dsh-agentic-pet README · Releasing：Every published version is reachable as tag `v<version>` — the tag, not the manifest, is what answers "what is on npm". Version in the tree therefore always equals the last *published* version.

dsh-agentic-pet README · Documentation：- Control-plane contract (the frozen consumer API every pet implementation speaks): see the multi-pet guide in the project documentation.
- Say-side TTS (BreezeBlue voice-over) design notes: `docs/tts.md` in the monorepo workspace (`packages/bundle/pet-app`).
- Known limitations and design notes live in the repo wiki and the project's engineering docs.
